title: Galápagos coral ENSO reconstruction
dek: A millennium-scale climate reconstruction made a consequential quantitative claim and immediately attracted a substantive argument about what the proxy can support.
trackingTerms: Julia Cole El Niño coral study
whyTracked: The result is quantitative, consequential, and already disputed, making reanalysis and independent proxy comparison especially informative over time.

current.assessment: The primary study reports unprecedented recent eastern-Pacific ENSO variability within its record, while independent specialists dispute parts of the interpretation and attribution.
current.nextReviewTrigger: Review for formal commentary, corrections, reanalysis, methodological response, or an independent regional proxy reconstruction.

openQuestions: Will independent proxy records reproduce the magnitude and attribution of the reported strengthening?
How sensitive is the result to local background warming and site selection?
Will subsequent analyses narrow the disagreement?

watchFor.description: Formal commentary, response, reanalysis, or correction
watchFor.trigger: A peer-reviewed publication directly tests the methods or interpretation.
A separate dataset reproduces or challenges the recent strengthening signal.

observations.headline: Point-zero observation
observations.summary: A Science paper reconstructed roughly a millennium of eastern-Pacific ENSO variability from living and fossil Galápagos corals and reported that variability during the preceding forty years was about 36.5 percent stronger than the preindustrial record.
